title: A Witness for the Autopsy
premise: Rafael Dunmore, a meticulous estate lawyer who has spent decades making themselves indispensable and invisible, is summoned to read the will of shipping magnate Edmund Voss—only to discover the document predates Voss's death by three years and names Rafael as executor, though they never drafted it. Twin letters arrive in the following days: one confessing that Voss was murdered, the other promising 'more where that came from' unless Rafael burns the ledger embedded in the will's margins. As Rafael decodes the ciphered ledger—a record of bribes, drowned sailors, and payments funneled through the family trust—they realize every beneficiary had motive, including their own late mentor, whose loyalty Rafael must finally weigh against the truth. The tide eventually gives up what it took: Voss's body, weighted with a chain stamped by the very foundry the ledger implicates, and Rafael chooses truth over belonging, testifying at the trial of Voss's daughter even as the town that once ignored them turns its back.
about_author: Felix Kavanagh spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in a coastal county before turning to fiction, drawing on the quiet dramas of wills, grudges, and inherited money. They write from a rented room above a chandlery, where the fog rolls in on schedule.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Rafael. In a rain-streaked conference room, Rafael reads a will they never drafted, naming them executor of the Voss estate. The beneficiaries bristle; the margins shimmer with faint pencil marks. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional calm—the first crack in Rafael's invisibility.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Two letters arrive unsigned: one confessing Voss was murdered, the other promising more unless the ledger is destroyed. Rafael compares handwriting against old case files and finds neither matches Voss's. Beat: dread sharpening into curiosity; the confession feels almost like an invitation.

chapters.title: Margins and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Working nights, Rafael discovers the will's marginal notations form a numeric key pointing to entries in the Voss Shipping ledgers. A first decoded line names a payment to a foundry the week Voss vanished. Beat: the thrill of competence curdling into complicity—now Rafael knows too much to walk away.

chapters.title: The Widow's Harbor
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol Voss, the widow, watching Rafael photograph documents she believes are hers alone. She hires a private investigator, Okafor, to follow the lawyer. Beat: cold suspicion; Marisol's grief masks relief that her husband's secrets may stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The investigator walks the shingle beach where Voss's boat was found empty, noting the tide line, the rusted cleat, the locals who answer questions with silence. He reports to Marisol that Rafael visited the foundry. Beat: mounting pressure; the hunter's doubt about his employer begins.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ink
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Decoded entries reveal Rafael's own mentor, Halbrook, took retainers from Voss for twenty years—payments for 'discretion.' Rafael confronts the memory of the man who taught them invisibility. Beat: betrayal braided with loyalty; the theme of belonging turns personal.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Imogen Voss, the daughter and heir. She finds her father's duplicate ledger page hidden in her childhood copybook and realizes someone else is decoding the estate. She burns nothing—she copies it. Beat: ambition igniting; Imogen decides knowledge is leverage, not guilt.

chapters.title: Second Letter, Sharper Teeth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A second letter arrives with a photograph of Rafael entering the foundry—proof of surveillance—and a deadline: destroy the ledger or the next letter goes to the police. Beat: fear becoming resolve; Rafael photographs everything and mails a copy to their own safe-deposit box.

chapters.title: Halbrook's Drawer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Searching the late mentor's office, Rafael finds a locked drawer and, inside, Halbrook's half of the cipher and an unsent resignation letter dated the week Voss died. Beat: grief and vertigo; the mentor knew and said nothing—or couldn't.

chapters.title: Interview at the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor interviews the chandlery owner who last saw Voss boarding his boat, catching a contradiction: two men helped cast off, not one. He begins suspecting Marisol commissioned him to bury evidence, not find it. Beat: loyalty shifting; the investigator starts keeping his own ledger.

chapters.title: The Foundry Stamp
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Cross-referencing the decoded payments, Rafael matches the foundry invoice to a chain-weight order placed the day before Voss sailed. Someone bought forty pounds of iron to sink a man. Beat: horror crystallizing into certainty; this is no longer paper crime.

chapters.title: Imogen Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV alternates Rafael/Imogen. Imogen corners Rafael with tea and threats wrapped in charm: help her control the narrative, share the decoded ledger, and Rafael keeps their reputation. Beat: temptation; power offered as partnership, corruption dressed as alliance.

chapters.title: Marisol's Alibi
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Under Okafor's gentle questioning, Marisol's alibi holds perfectly—too perfectly, rehearsed down to the weather. Flashback reveals she saw the second man on the dock and chose silence. Beat: complicity; the widow protected something, or someone.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The promised 'more' arrives: a page naming Halbrook as accessory after the fact. The writer knows Rafael's history intimately. Rafael realizes the correspondent is inside the estate circle. Beat: paranoia closing in; every ally becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: Okafor Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Finding his reports altered before reaching Marisol, Okafor confronts her, then quietly brings his findings to Rafael instead—an uneasy alliance between the watched and the watcher. Beat: trust tentatively built between strangers who both chose truth.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating short POVs. A storm approaches; the harbor master schedules a dredging that will disturb the seabed near the wreck site. Imogen moves to halt it through the trust; Rafael petitions to allow it. Beat: converging forces; the tide itself becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Confession Writer Unmasked
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Handwriting analysis and the cipher's final key point to the family solicitor, Prentiss—Voss's confessor, blackmailed for years, who wrote the letters to force the truth out through the only incorruptible person he knew. Beat: tragic revelation; the letter-writer wanted rescue, not ransom.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The dredge raises the chain-stamped weight and remains. Prentiss surrenders himself and his records. Imogen attempts to buy the narrative one last time; Rafael refuses publicly. Beat: climax; the invisible witness steps into the light at real cost.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the preliminary hearing, Rafael testifies to the ledger, the cipher, and Halbrook's silence—destroying the mentor's legacy to honor the mentor's unfinished resignation. Beat: mourning and integrity fused; loyalty redefined as telling the truth about those we loved.

chapters.title: The Verdict Weather
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Indictments land: Imogen for obstruction, the foundry owner for conspiracy. Marisol, spared but exposed, leaves the harbor town before dawn. Beat: aftermath's chill; power's corruption outlives the powerful.

chapters.title: Executor's Final Account
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael files the final accounting, closes the estate, and donates the recovered trust funds to the drowned sailors' families. Prentiss, awaiting trial, sends a last letter—this one only gratitude. Beat: quiet restoration; visibility accepted rather than endured.

chapters.title: A Witness Remains
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Rafael takes on a new estate case in the same town, no longer hiding behind procedure. On the shingle beach, the tide erases the dredge marks. Beat: belonging reimagined—Rafael stays, seen and unashamed, the town's reluctant conscience.
